trips.title: Everest Base Camp Trek
trips.accommodation: Hotel in Kathmandu, teahouses on trek
trips.summary: Trek through Sherpa villages and the Khumbu glacier to the foot of the world’s highest mountain, with sunrise over Everest from Kala Patthar.
overview: The Everest Base Camp Trek is the most famous trek in Nepal. After a thrilling mountain flight to Lukla, you follow the Dudh Koshi valley to Namche Bazaar, the Sherpa capital, and continue past Tengboche Monastery to the high villages of Dingboche and Lobuche.

Two acclimatization days are built in to help your body adjust to the altitude. The highlight is standing at Everest Base Camp (5,364 m) and climbing Kala Patthar (5,545 m) for the best close-up view of Everest, Lhotse and Nuptse.
highlights: Scenic flight to Tenzing-Hillary Airport, Lukla
Namche Bazaar and Sherpa culture
Tengboche Monastery with Ama Dablam views
Everest Base Camp and the Khumbu Icefall
Sunrise over Everest from Kala Patthar (5,545 m)

faqs.question: How difficult is the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: It is a challenging trek because of the altitude, not technical difficulty. You walk 5–7 hours a day; anyone with good fitness and some hiking experience can complete it with proper acclimatization.

faqs.question: What is the best time for the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (March–May) and autumn (September–November) offer the most stable weather and clearest mountain views.

faqs.question: Do I need travel insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Insurance covering trekking up to 6,000 m and helicopter evacuation is mandatory for this trip.

trips.title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
trips.accommodation: Hotels in Kathmandu & Pokhara, teahouses on trek
trips.summary: Walk through Gurung villages and bamboo forests into the Annapurna Sanctuary, a ring of 7,000–8,000 m peaks around Annapurna Base Camp.
overview: The Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) Trek takes you from the lakeside city of Pokhara into the Annapurna Sanctuary, a glacial basin surrounded by Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) and Hiunchuli.
It is shorter and lower than the Everest trek, making it ideal for first-time Himalayan trekkers. The return route passes the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda.

Close-up views of sacred Machhapuchhre
Traditional Gurung village of Chhomrong
Natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda

faqs.question: Is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek good for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes. With a maximum altitude of 4,130 m and good teahouses, ABC is one of the best first Himalayan treks for fit beginners.

faqs.question: Can I trek to ABC in the monsoon?
faqs.answer: It is possible but trails are slippery and views are often cloudy. We recommend spring or autumn.

trips.accommodation: Hotel in Kathmandu, teahouses on trek
trips.summary: A remote, off-the-beaten-path circuit around Manaslu (8,163 m), crossing the Larkya La pass through Tibetan-Buddhist villages.
overview: The Manaslu Circuit is a restricted-area trek that circles the world’s eighth highest mountain. It combines subtropical river valleys with high alpine villages like Samagaun and Samdo.
The crossing of the Larkya La (5,106 m) is one of the most dramatic pass crossings in Nepal, with views of Himlung, Cheo Himal and Annapurna II.

posts.title: Best Time to Trek in Nepal: A Season-by-Season Guide
posts.excerpt: Spring and autumn are the classic trekking seasons, but winter and monsoon have their own rewards. Here is how to choose the right month for your trek.
posts.author: Kiteice Team

sections.heading: Autumn (September–November)
paragraphs: Autumn is the most popular trekking season in Nepal. The monsoon rains clear the dust from the air, giving crisp mountain views and stable weather. Trails and teahouses are busiest in October.

sections.heading: Spring (March–May)
paragraphs: Spring brings warmer temperatures and rhododendron forests in full bloom. It is also Everest expedition season, so base camp is full of climbers’ tents.

sections.heading: Winter and monsoon
paragraphs: Winter (December–February) is cold at altitude but quiet and clear – ideal for lower treks like Langtang or Ghorepani. Monsoon (June–August) is wet in most regions, but rain-shadow areas like Upper Mustang are excellent.

posts.title: How to Prepare for the Everest Base Camp Trek
posts.excerpt: A practical training plan, packing tips and altitude advice to help you reach Everest Base Camp feeling strong.
posts.author: Kiteice Team

sections.heading: Start training 8–12 weeks before
paragraphs: Focus on cardio endurance: hiking with a loaded backpack, stair climbing, cycling and running. Aim for at least one long hike of 5–6 hours per week in the last month.

sections.heading: Pack light but smart
paragraphs: Porters carry up to 10–12 kg per trekker. Bring layers rather than bulky items: thermal base layers, a fleece, a down jacket, a waterproof shell and a good sleeping bag rated to –10 °C.

sections.heading: Respect the altitude
paragraphs: Walk slowly, drink 3–4 litres of water a day and use the acclimatization days. Tell your guide about any headache, nausea or dizziness straight away.

posts.title: Altitude Sickness: Symptoms and Prevention Tips for Trekkers
posts.excerpt: Acute Mountain Sickness can affect anyone above 2,500 m. Learn the warning signs and the simple rules that keep you safe in the Himalayas.
posts.author: Kiteice Team

sections.heading: Know the symptoms
paragraphs: Common early symptoms of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) are headache, loss of appetite, nausea, fatigue and poor sleep. Serious forms (HAPE and HACE) cause breathlessness at rest, confusion and loss of coordination and need immediate descent.

sections.heading: Golden rules
paragraphs: Above 3,000 m, increase your sleeping altitude by no more than 300–500 m per day, take a rest day every 3–4 days, and never go higher with symptoms. Consult your doctor before the trip about medication such as acetazolamide.
